title: Windows 8 logo
lede: Pentagram’s 2012 Windows logo: the waving four-color flag redrawn as a flat, single-color window in perspective.
summary: Four flat light-blue panes in perspective beside a plain sans-serif wordmark. Pentagram for Microsoft, 2012.

evidence.note: Inspected a 1920 × 420 render of [File:Windows logo and wordmark - 2012–2015.svg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Windows_logo_and_wordmark_-_2012%E2%80%932015.svg) and stored a 1600 px copy. Pentagram’s project page read on 2026-09-28; it lists Paula Scher as partner.

styles.note: Clear: the brand mark itself drops gradient, gloss, and the four colors for one flat hue, and Pentagram ties it to Metro’s “authentically digital” rule.

context: Pentagram writes that the Windows logo gained “a 3D effect with a gradient” for Windows XP and became a “pearl” for Vista, and that the new logo “reflects the sleek, modern ‘Metro’ design language”.

Pentagram: “One guideline of Metro is that the graphic or interface must appear ‘authentically digital’ – that is, it should not appear to be material or three-dimensional using gradients or effects.” The logo instead “suggests dimensionality using the classic principle of perspective”.
Commons dates the logo to February 2012, with the Windows 8 Consumer Preview.
observed: Four panes of one flat light blue form a window seen in perspective: the left panes are shorter and narrower than the right panes.
A white cross of even width separates the panes.
The wordmark “Windows” is a plain humanist sans-serif in the same blue, with no effects.
interpretation: Measured with `tools/image-traits.py`; see the measurement file. The logo shows the rule of the style at the scale of a brand mark: depth by drawing (perspective), never by rendering (gradient or shadow).
Compare the gradients and glossy orbs of the Aero era in [Windows 7](ref:windows-7-aero-interface).
borrow: When a flat mark needs depth, draw it with geometry, such as perspective or overlap, and keep each shape one solid color.

images.alt: Windows logo of 2012: four light-blue panes forming a window in perspective, separated by a white cross, beside the word Windows in the same blue.
images.caption: Windows logo and wordmark, 2012–2015, from [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Windows_logo_and_wordmark_-_2012%E2%80%932015.svg) (PD-textlogo).

rights.statement: Wikimedia Commons tags the logo {{PD-textlogo}}: simple geometric shapes and text, below the threshold of originality in the United States. It is a Microsoft trademark; it appears here only to identify and discuss the design.
